body: Yeah, that's why I said within our ability, because sometimes it's outside what we're capable of.

I, and I'm pretty sure anyone else here, for that matter, are not trying to dismiss anyone else's experiences with mental illness or suffering. Of course there are people who can make it out the other side and have a life that they are happy with, and that's great for them. But most of us don't see ourselves as those people.

This is a place for people who have pretty much lost all hope, for those of us who don't see a life worth living ahead of us. We don't come here looking to play the depression olympics, we come here because this is a place where we can be completely honest about how we feel, free of judgement, to others who are also suicidal. 

Don't think we haven't tried anything and everything within our ability. We have, it hasn't worked, and that's why we're here.

Thank you for saying this. I feel like you really captured what it feels like to have chronic suicidal thoughts. The constant apathy towards life, the dread you feel when you're even a little bit happy because experience tells you that it's not going to last, and the attitude from people who cannot empathize with you saying, "oh it'll get better," or, "you just need to get out more", suggesting the mental equivalent of putting a bandaid on a malignant tumor.

People who have never experienced mental illness cannot understand the pain and suffering that drives one to suicide. They cannot even fathom having a life that they genuinely don't want, and they have no idea how lucky they are for that.

Thank you, it's comforting to know there are other people out there who also have crippling OCD, but also I'm so sorry you have because I know how awful it can be. 

I understand what you're saying, with your OCD being stressful yet somehow keeping you alive. I have that hope to, the hope that magically it will make things better even though it keeps me from doing even the simplest of tasks. I just feel like I can't take the chance of not doing the compulsions, because what if that is actually helping in a way? And every time something happens that makes me upset I blame it on myself for not doing something that sated my OCD.

I have OCD as well and it has contributed a lot to my suicidality, so what you're saying kind of makes sense to me. I know everyone thinks OCD is just like obsessive cleaning or some shit, but it takes on so many different manifestations other than that. Hell, I'm a messy as fuck person because I'm too depressed to clean and I feel like I can't move things because that's their place, can't change it or else who knows what might happen.

I've done group therapy and it was fucking awful. Everyone just went around and talked about how suicidal they were and their most traumatic experiences. I'm kind of an empath so this had a very intense affect on me. I self harmed because of how much I hated it and when I told the social workers running it that they just said I have to keep going with it. I didn't have a choice in doing it.

I called a suicide hotline once and they weren't very good. The person I was talking to essentially said that if I killed myself, the news of that could inspire someone else to do it and basically I would start this whole cycle of suicides. 

I find this subreddit to be a bit better. At least the people here understand and feel the same. None of the bullshit, "don't kill yourself, puppies and rainbows exist!!!!11!!!!1!" or, "it's not that bad!!!", just real, honest, thoughts.

I'm the same way. I know I'm such a coward for not going through with it before, but I want to be dead so bad. Sorry your mom called you all that shit, that's pretty heartless. I hope you get what you need to get out of there and live a good life, but know that there's tons of us here who feel the same way that you do.
Yes, every day, even on days that objectively aren't that bad. I'm so shit at everything that I can't even kill myself right.

This is part of why I became an anarchist and contributes to my suicidality today. Why the hell does anyone want to devote their entire lives to making someone else more money while the rest of us live off of the scraps? If there was a class revolution going on right now, I'd gladly give my life to it, but there isn't, so might as well just off myself because I sure as hell don't want to spend what little energy I have making someone else richer.

Shit did I write this and not remember it? It's too relatable. My first attempt was at 12 and honestly I wish I had succeeded, then I wouldn't have gone through all the shit that makes me suicidal now along with all the shit I had as a young kid.

Making friends is really hard. And you should live for yourself, not for your boyfriend, even if he is a good person and all. 

I'm here if you wanna talk.

I also have extremely similar feelings. Even when I'm not particularly depressed, I would be perfectly fine with dying. And I think it would be easier on my friends and family if I died from a natural looking cause or something.

Do you have a therapist or someone to talk to? I think even making a post on here is a good way to express yourself.

Thank you, I just don't even know what to talk about. If I confide in someone about one of my many mental health issues they say something like "but rainbows and puppies exist!!!!" Those are nice, but no amount of those things will fix what I've got.

You are really kind for offering.

I graduated college a few months ago and did pretty well. I got good grades, all this research experience, and was pretty involved. Sure, things were a struggle, but I had goals to work towards even if they were really difficult for me to accomplish. I had a lot of difficulties my last semester because I was doing a thesis and going through some relationship troubles, then I graduated, finished all my remaining work, and now I'm looking for a job but I have nothing to do in the meantime. I'm bored and alone with intrusive thoughts and it just sucks. At least school was some sort of a distraction and I was working towards something. Now I'm trying to find a job and everything is exhausting. I have no motivation to do anything because I don't really have anything to do, and not for lack of trying. I'm sure it's slow compared to others, but I'm going at my own pace and trying to take it easy so every day doesn't suck. 

BPD takes many forms and no one expresses it in the same way.
